As the [National Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Olympic_Committee "National Olympic Committee") (NOC) for the United Kingdom, the [British Olympic Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Olympic_Association "British Olympic Association") (BOA) membership encompasses the four [Home Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_Nations "Home Nations") of the United Kingdom ([England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England "England"), [Northern Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland "Northern Ireland"), [Scotland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scotland "Scotland") and [Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wales "Wales"), who notably compete separately in many international sports outside Olympic competition for historic reasons), plus the three [Crown Dependencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_Dependencies "Crown Dependencies") ([Guernsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bailiwick_of_Guernsey "Bailiwick of Guernsey"), [Isle of Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isle_of_Man "Isle of Man") and [Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jersey "Jersey")), and all but three of the [British Overseas Territories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Overseas_Territories "British Overseas Territories")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-3)([Bermuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bermuda_at_the_Olympics "Bermuda at the Olympics"), [British Virgin Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Virgin_Islands_at_the_Olympics "British Virgin Islands at the Olympics") and [Cayman Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cayman_Islands_at_the_Olympics "Cayman Islands at the Olympics") have their own NOCs).

Representatives of the [devolved Northern Ireland government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland_Executive "Northern Ireland Executive") and others in the region have objected to the name "Team GB" as discriminatory and called for it to be renamed as "Team UK" to make it clearer that Northern Ireland is included on the team.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-4)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-5)

Under the IOC charter, the [Olympic Federation of Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Federation_of_Ireland "Olympic Federation of Ireland") is also responsible for the entire island of [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland "Ireland").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-6) However, athletes from [Northern Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland "Northern Ireland") can elect to represent either Great Britain or [Ireland at the Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland_at_the_Olympics "Ireland at the Olympics"), as [people of Northern Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_of_Northern_Ireland "People of Northern Ireland"). A number of Northern Irish-born athletes, particularly in boxing, have won medals for Ireland at the Games, while a small number of athletes from Northern Ireland have represented both Team GB and Team Ireland, most recently swimming gold medallist [Jack McMillan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_McMillan_(swimmer) "Jack McMillan (swimmer)").

Usually most of Northern Ireland's athletes at the Olympics compete for Team Ireland. At the [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics"), 6 athletes (16%) from Northern Ireland, represented Great Britain, while 31 athletes (84%) represented Ireland.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-7) In 2016, eight represented Great Britain and 21 represented Ireland.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-8)

All athletes from the whole of [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland "Ireland") were included in the Great Britain team up until the 1920 Olympics as the entire island was part of the United Kingdom at that time. Hence the Team GB claim to have won at least one gold at every Summer Games is partially founded on a single Irish athlete, [Tom Kiely](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Kiely "Tom Kiely"), who won gold in the [1904 St. Louis games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1904_St._Louis_Games "1904 St. Louis Games"). While Kiely himself objected to the designation, considering himself simply Irish, Olympic historians recognise his medal as won by Great Britain and Ireland, thus maintaining the unique British record.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-9)

The existence of a Great Britain team has been criticised by [Welsh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welsh_nationalism "Welsh nationalism") and [Scottish nationalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_nationalists "Scottish nationalists"), advocating for separate [Welsh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_in_Wales#Calls_for_Wales_Olympic_team "Sport in Wales")[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-:0-10) and [Scottish Olympic teams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campaign_for_a_Scottish_Olympic_Team "Campaign for a Scottish Olympic Team") instead.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-11)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-13)

Other nations that formed part of the then [British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire"), however, were represented separately even before full independence in a variety of ways, either as fledgling nations such as [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa_at_the_Olympics "South Africa at the Olympics") and [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_at_the_Olympics "India at the Olympics"), or occasionally in regional teams such as [Australasia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australasia_at_the_Olympics "Australasia at the Olympics") and British [West Indies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_West_Indies_at_the_1960_Summer_Olympics "British West Indies at the 1960 Summer Olympics").

## Hosted games

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Great_Britain_at_the_Olympics&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Hosted games")]

The United Kingdom has hosted the Summer Games on three occasions – 1908, 1948 and 2012, all in London – second only to the United States. At the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics") in Rio, [Great Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Britain_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Great Britain at the 2016 Summer Olympics") became the first team to win more medals at a Summer Olympics immediately after hosting a Summer Olympics; they won 67 medals overall, coming in second place in the medal table ahead of [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "China at the 2016 Summer Olympics"), two more than in [London in 2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics"). This success came 20 years after finishing 36th in the medal table, after winning just one gold and fourteen other medals at the [1996 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Summer_Olympics "1996 Summer Olympics") in Atlanta, which led to significant changes in the management and funding of British sports and facilities.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-14)

[London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") also won the right to host the 1944 Summer Olympics. However, the 1944 games were cancelled due to the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War").

### Potential future bids

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Great_Britain_at_the_Olympics&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Potential future bids")]

In February 2019, the [Mayor of London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_London "Mayor of London")[Sadiq Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sadiq_Khan "Sadiq Khan") announced plans to bid for the [2032](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2032_Summer_Olympics "2032 Summer Olympics") or 2036 Olympics, which was backed by [UK Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Sport "UK Sport").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-15) However, it has been speculated that either [Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester "Manchester") or [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham "Birmingham") may be in the frame to host future games, rather than London. In July 2021, the 2032 Games were awarded to [Brisbane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brisbane "Brisbane").

In July 2024, Khan revealed he was to attend the opening ceremony of the [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics") in Paris and would use the opportunity to lobby members of the British Olympic Association and the [Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_the_United_Kingdom "Prime Minister of the United Kingdom") (a potential bid would need to be both underwritten by the government and backed by the BOA) into hosting the 2040 Olympics.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-16) He claimed London could host the "greenest games ever" by reusing venues from the 2012 games including the London Stadium, the London Aquatics Centre, Lee Valley Velopark and Copper Box Arena. The idea was backed by [Tom Daley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Daley "Tom Daley"), Team GB diver, commenting that "London is one of the few cities on the planet where you would be able to host the games tomorrow".

A 2025 proposal by the Heseltine Institute would see Manchester and [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool "Liverpool") launch a joint bid for the 2040 Games - this idea was backed by the Mayor of Greater Manchester [Andy Burnham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Burnham "Andy Burnham"), who described the prospect of the two cities hosting the games as an opportunity to 'rebalance the country'.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-17)

Notes
*   **NAT**Australian [Frederick Lane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_Lane "Frederick Lane") competed at the [1900 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1900_Summer_Olympics "1900 Summer Olympics"), winning two gold medals in the [swimming events](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_1900_Summer_Olympics "Swimming at the 1900 Summer Olympics"). As a representative of a British club, his participation and medals were attributed accordingly.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-21)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-22)Conversely, British [Lloyd Hildebrand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_Hildebrand "Lloyd Hildebrand") won a silver medal in the [25 km cycling event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cycling_at_the_1900_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_25_kilometres "Cycling at the 1900 Summer Olympics – Men's 25 kilometres"). As a representative of a French club, his participation and medal were attributed to France.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-23)
*   **MIX**At the 1900 Summer Olympics [four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1900_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#Team_events "1900 Summer Olympics medal table") team event medals (3 gold and 1 silver) won by British clubs competing as [mixed teams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_teams_at_the_Olympics "Mixed teams at the Olympics")—composed primarily of British athletes alongside a few non-British participants—were attributed to Great Britain: gold in the [5000 metres team race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_1900_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_5000_metres_team_race "Athletics at the 1900 Summer Olympics – Men's 5000 metres team race"), [polo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polo_at_the_1900_Summer_Olympics "Polo at the 1900 Summer Olympics"), and [water polo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_polo_at_the_1900_Summer_Olympics "Water polo at the 1900 Summer Olympics") and silver in polo.
*   **ART**[Art competitions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_competitions_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Art competitions at the Summer Olympics") (1912–1948) are not included in the medal table above, as they were [non-sports events](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_sports#Feats_and_artistic_events "Olympic sports") formerly part of the Olympic Games.[[nb 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-art-24)Great Britain won a total of nine art competition medals (3 gold, 5 silver and 1 bronze), across the [1920](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_competitions_at_the_1920_Summer_Olympics "Art competitions at the 1920 Summer Olympics"), [1924](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_competitions_at_the_1924_Summer_Olympics "Art competitions at the 1924 Summer Olympics"), [1928](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_competitions_at_the_1928_Summer_Olympics "Art competitions at the 1928 Summer Olympics"), [1932](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_competitions_at_the_1932_Summer_Olympics "Art competitions at the 1932 Summer Olympics") and [1948 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_competitions_at_the_1948_Summer_Olympics "Art competitions at the 1948 Summer Olympics").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-olympics_gbr-19)

[Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia"), referred to by its formal name; the Russian Federation, by the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee"), has competed at the modern [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games") on many occasions, but as different nations in its history. As the [Russian Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Empire "Russian Empire"), the nation first competed at the [1900 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1900_Summer_Olympics "1900 Summer Olympics") and returned again in 1908 and 1912. It would be forty years until Russian athletes once again competed at the Olympics, as the [Soviet Union at the 1952 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union_at_the_1952_Summer_Olympics "Soviet Union at the 1952 Summer Olympics"). After the [dissolution of the Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Soviet_Union "Dissolution of the Soviet Union") in 1991, Russia competed as part of the [Unified Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unified_Team_at_the_Olympics "Unified Team at the Olympics") in 1992, and finally returned once again as _Russia_ at the [1994 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Winter_Olympics "1994 Winter Olympics").

The [Russian Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Olympic_Committee "Russian Olympic Committee") was created in 1991 and recognized in 1993. The Soviet Union hosted the [1980 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Summer_Olympics "1980 Summer Olympics") in [Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow "Moscow"), and the Russian Federation hosted the [2014 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Winter_Olympics "2014 Winter Olympics") in [Sochi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sochi "Sochi").

In twelve appearances from 1994 to 2016, Russian athletes won a total of 422 medals at the [Summer Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympic_Games "Summer Olympic Games") and another 120 at the [Winter Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter_Olympic_Games "Winter Olympic Games"). Russia's 542 total medals, including 193 gold medals, are second behind only the United States in that timespan.

In 2017, Russia was suspended from competing at the Olympic Games due to the [state-sponsored doping scandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doping_in_Russia "Doping in Russia"). Russian athletes were allowed to participate in the [2018 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Winter_Olympics "2018 Winter Olympics") as the [Olympic Athletes from Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Athletes_from_Russia_at_the_2018_Winter_Olympics "Olympic Athletes from Russia at the 2018 Winter Olympics") (OAR). They were also allowed to compete at the [2020 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics "2020 Summer Olympics") and the [2022 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Winter_Olympics "2022 Winter Olympics"), representing the [Russian Olympic Committee (ROC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Olympic_Committee_athletes_at_the_Olympics "Russian Olympic Committee athletes at the Olympics").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-ioc_suspendes_russian_noc-1)

Amid the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine"), the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") (IOC) allowed Russian athletes to participate at the [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics") and [2026 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Winter_Olympics "2026 Winter Olympics") as [Individual Neutral Athletes (AIN)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Individual_Neutral_Athletes "Individual Neutral Athletes").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-insidethegames_3_Feb-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-ReutersMay2025-3) The suspension of the ROC was provisionally lifted in July 2026, before the qualifying events for the [2028 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2028_Summer_Olympics "2028 Summer Olympics"), with the IOC also stating that a decision on restoring the complete use of the Russia name and its national symbols at the Olympics will later be made "at the appropriate time."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-Olympics.com-2026-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-Politico-2026-5)

## Notes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Russia_at_the_Olympics&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Notes")]

*   On 9 February 2014, Russia captured the inaugural gold medal in the team figure skating event at the [2014 Sochi Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Sochi_Winter_Olympics "2014 Sochi Winter Olympics").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-12)[Yulia Lipnitskaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yulia_Lipnitskaya "Yulia Lipnitskaya"), at 15, becomes the youngest Russian Winter Olympic medalist.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
*   On 10 February 2014, [Viktor Ahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viktor_Ahn "Viktor Ahn") won the first short track speedskating medal for Russia competing as Russia. He won the bronze medal in the 1500m short track speedskating event at the [2014 Sochi winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Sochi_winter_Olympics "2014 Sochi winter Olympics").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-UTSD-2014-02-10-13)
*   On 15 February 2014, Ahn won the second Russian gold medal in the 1000m short track speedskating event, leading the first Russian 1–2 finish in short track, with [Vladimir Grigorev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Grigorev "Vladimir Grigorev") winning silver. At 31 years and 191 days, Grigorev also became the oldest man to win a short track Olympic medal.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-14)
*   On 20 February 2014, [Adelina Sotnikova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelina_Sotnikova "Adelina Sotnikova") won the first ever Russian ladies figure skating gold medal.

## Stripped Olympic medals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Russia_at_the_Olympics&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Stripped Olympic medals")]

See also: [List of stripped Olympic medals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stripped_Olympic_medals "List of stripped Olympic medals") and [Doping in Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doping_in_Russia "Doping in Russia")

Due to doping violations, Russia has been stripped of 52 Olympic medals – the most of any country, four times the number of the runner-up, and 31% of the global total. It was the leading country in terms of medals removed due to doping at the [2002 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Winter_Olympics "2002 Winter Olympics") (5 medals), the [2006 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Winter_Olympics "2006 Winter Olympics") (1 medal), the [2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics") (14 medals), the [2010 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Winter_Olympics "2010 Winter Olympics") (2 medals), the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics") (20 medals), [2014 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Winter_Olympics "2014 Winter Olympics") (4 medals — 10 others were stripped and subsequently returned), as well as joint-most at the [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics") (3 medals) and the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics") (1 medal). Also two medals were also stripped from Russian teams competing as [OAR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Athletes_from_Russia_at_the_2018_Winter_Olympics "Olympic Athletes from Russia at the 2018 Winter Olympics") at the [2018 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Winter_Olympics "2018 Winter Olympics") (1 medal) and the [ROC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Olympic_Committee_athletes_at_the_Olympics "Russian Olympic Committee athletes at the Olympics") at the [2022 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Winter_Olympics "2022 Winter Olympics") (1 medal downgraded from gold → bronze).

## 2016–2026 suspension

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Russia_at_the_Olympics&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2016–2026 suspension")]

Main articles: [Doping in Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doping_in_Russia "Doping in Russia"), [International sporting sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_sporting_sanctions_during_the_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "International sporting sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine"), and [Concerns and controversies at the 2024 Summer Olympics §Participation of Russian and Belarusian athletes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concerns_and_controversies_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics#Participation_of_Russian_and_Belarusian_athletes "Concerns and controversies at the 2024 Summer Olympics")

Russia was partially banned from participation at the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics") due to the [state-sponsored doping scandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doping_in_Russia "Doping in Russia"). Russian athletes were then allowed to participate in the [2018 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Winter_Olympics "2018 Winter Olympics") as the Olympic Athletes from Russia (OAR), and in both the [2020 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics "2020 Summer Olympics") and the [2022 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Winter_Olympics "2022 Winter Olympics") as the [Russian Olympic Committee athletes (ROC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Olympic_Committee_athletes_at_the_Olympics "Russian Olympic Committee athletes at the Olympics").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-64)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-ioc_suspendes_russian_noc-1)

Amid the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine"), the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") (IOC) announced in January 2023 plans to have Russian athletes introduced as [Individual Neutral Athletes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Individual_Neutral_Athletes "Individual Neutral Athletes") (AIN) at the [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-insidethegames_3_Feb-2)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-65) The IOC also published a statement stating that it supported the return of Russian athletes, as long as they did not "actively" advocate for the war and as long as their flag, anthem, colors, and organizations were excluded (thus preventing them from competing under the Russian Olympic Committee as in 2020 and 2022).[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-66) However, they could not compete in team events.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-67) With the Russo-Ukrainian war extending into 2026, Russian athletes were also introduced as [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia"), referred to by its formal name; the Russian Federation, by the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee"), has competed at the modern [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games") on many occasions, but as different nations in its history. As the [Russian Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Empire "Russian Empire"), the nation first competed at the [1900 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1900_Summer_Olympics "1900 Summer Olympics") and returned again in 1908 and 1912. It would be forty years until Russian athletes once again competed at the Olympics, as the [Soviet Union at the 1952 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union_at_the_1952_Summer_Olympics "Soviet Union at the 1952 Summer Olympics"). After the [dissolution of the Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Soviet_Union "Dissolution of the Soviet Union") in 1991, Russia competed as part of the [Unified Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unified_Team_at_the_Olympics "Unified Team at the Olympics") in 1992, and finally returned once again as _Russia_ at the [1994 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Winter_Olympics "1994 Winter Olympics").

The [Russian Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Olympic_Committee "Russian Olympic Committee") was created in 1991 and recognized in 1993. The Soviet Union hosted the [1980 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Summer_Olympics "1980 Summer Olympics") in [Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow "Moscow"), and the Russian Federation hosted the [2014 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Winter_Olympics "2014 Winter Olympics") in [Sochi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sochi "Sochi").

In twelve appearances from 1994 to 2016, Russian athletes won a total of 422 medals at the [Summer Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympic_Games "Summer Olympic Games") and another 120 at the [Winter Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter_Olympic_Games "Winter Olympic Games"). Russia's 542 total medals, including 193 gold medals, are second behind only the United States in that timespan.

In 2017, Russia was suspended from competing at the Olympic Games due to the [state-sponsored doping scandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doping_in_Russia "Doping in Russia"). Russian athletes were allowed to participate in the [2018 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Winter_Olympics "2018 Winter Olympics") as the [Olympic Athletes from Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Athletes_from_Russia_at_the_2018_Winter_Olympics "Olympic Athletes from Russia at the 2018 Winter Olympics") (OAR). They were also allowed to compete at the [2020 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics "2020 Summer Olympics") and the [2022 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Winter_Olympics "2022 Winter Olympics"), representing the [Russian Olympic Committee (ROC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Olympic_Committee_athletes_at_the_Olympics "Russian Olympic Committee athletes at the Olympics").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-ioc_suspendes_russian_noc-1)

Amid the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine"), the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") (IOC) allowed Russian athletes to participate at the [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics") and [2026 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Winter_Olympics "2026 Winter Olympics") as [Individual Neutral Athletes (AIN)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Individual_Neutral_Athletes "Individual Neutral Athletes").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-insidethegames_3_Feb-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-ReutersMay2025-3) The suspension of the ROC was provisionally lifted in July 2026, before the qualifying events for the [2028 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2028_Summer_Olympics "2028 Summer Olympics"), with the IOC also stating that a decision on restoring the complete use of the Russia name and its national symbols at the Olympics will later be made "at the appropriate time."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-Olympics.com-2026-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-Politico-2026-5)

## Hosted Games

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Russia_at_the_Olympics&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Hosted Games")]

Moscow was the host of the 1980 Summer Games, when Russia ([Russian SFSR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Soviet_Federative_Socialist_Republic "Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic")) was part of the Soviet Union. Sochi was the host of the 2014 Winter Games, as part of the Russian Federation.

## Notes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Russia_at_the_Olympics&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Notes")]

*   On 9 February 2014, Russia captured the inaugural gold medal in the team figure skating event at the [2014 Sochi Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Sochi_Winter_Olympics "2014 Sochi Winter Olympics").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-12)[Yulia Lipnitskaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yulia_Lipnitskaya "Yulia Lipnitskaya"), at 15, becomes the youngest Russian Winter Olympic medalist.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
*   On 10 February 2014, [Viktor Ahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viktor_Ahn "Viktor Ahn") won the first short track speedskating medal for Russia competing as Russia. He won the bronze medal in the 1500m short track speedskating event at the [2014 Sochi winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Sochi_winter_Olympics "2014 Sochi winter Olympics").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-UTSD-2014-02-10-13)
*   On 15 February 2014, Ahn won the second Russian gold medal in the 1000m short track speedskating event, leading the first Russian 1–2 finish in short track, with [Vladimir Grigorev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Grigorev "Vladimir Grigorev") winning silver. At 31 years and 191 days, Grigorev also became the oldest man to win a short track Olympic medal.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-14)
*   On 20 February 2014, [Adelina Sotnikova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelina_Sotnikova "Adelina Sotnikova") won the first ever Russian ladies figure skating gold medal.

## Stripped Olympic medals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Russia_at_the_Olympics&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Stripped Olympic medals")]

See also: [List of stripped Olympic medals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stripped_Olympic_medals "List of stripped Olympic medals") and [Doping in Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doping_in_Russia "Doping in Russia")

Due to doping violations, Russia has been stripped of 52 Olympic medals – the most of any country, four times the number of the runner-up, and 31% of the global total. It was the leading country in terms of medals removed due to doping at the [2002 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Winter_Olympics "2002 Winter Olympics") (5 medals), the [2006 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Winter_Olympics "2006 Winter Olympics") (1 medal), the [2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics") (14 medals), the [2010 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Winter_Olympics "2010 Winter Olympics") (2 medals), the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics") (20 medals), [2014 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Winter_Olympics "2014 Winter Olympics") (4 medals — 10 others were stripped and subsequently returned), as well as joint-most at the [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics") (3 medals) and the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics") (1 medal). Also two medals were also stripped from Russian teams competing as [OAR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Athletes_from_Russia_at_the_2018_Winter_Olympics "Olympic Athletes from Russia at the 2018 Winter Olympics") at the [2018 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Winter_Olympics "2018 Winter Olympics") (1 medal) and the [ROC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Olympic_Committee_athletes_at_the_Olympics "Russian Olympic Committee athletes at the Olympics") at the [2022 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Winter_Olympics "2022 Winter Olympics") (1 medal downgraded from gold → bronze).

[Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran "Iran"), formerly known as [Persia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Name_of_Iran "Name of Iran") before 1935 and officially the Islamic Republic of Iran since 1979, first participated in the [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games") in [1900](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_at_the_1900_Summer_Olympics "Iran at the 1900 Summer Olympics"). Iran has sent athletes to compete in every [Summer Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympic_Games "Summer Olympic Games") since [1948](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_at_the_1948_Summer_Olympics "Iran at the 1948 Summer Olympics"), except for [1980](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Summer_Olympics_boycott "1980 Summer Olympics boycott") and [1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Summer_Olympics_boycott "1984 Summer Olympics boycott") due to [political boycotts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boycott "Boycott"). Iran has also participated in the [Winter Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter_Olympic_Games "Winter Olympic Games") on several occasions since [1956](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_at_the_1956_Winter_Olympics "Iran at the 1956 Winter Olympics").

Iran has participated in 19 Summer Olympics and 13 Winter Olympics so far. Iran participated in 9 Summer Olympics and gained 4 gold medals before the [1979 Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iranian_Revolution "Iranian Revolution"), and participated in 10 Summer Olympics and won 23 gold medals after the revolution.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-2)

[Freydoun Malkom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freydoun_Malkom "Freydoun Malkom"), a [fencer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fencing "Fencing") who competed in the [épée](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89p%C3%A9e_(fencing) "Épée (fencing)") event at the [1900 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_at_the_1900_Summer_Olympics "Iran at the 1900 Summer Olympics"), was the first [Iranian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran "Iran") Olympic competitor. [Jafar Salmasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jafar_Salmasi "Jafar Salmasi") won Iran's first Olympic medal in [1948](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_at_the_1948_Summer_Olympics "Iran at the 1948 Summer Olympics"), and [Kimia Alizadeh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimia_Alizadeh "Kimia Alizadeh") was the first Iranian female Olympic medalist, having done so in [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Iran at the 2016 Summer Olympics"). Iranian athletes have won a total of 88 Summer Olympic medals, all in [wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amateur_wrestling "Amateur wrestling"), [weightlifting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_weightlifting "Olympic weightlifting"), [taekwondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taekwondo "Taekwondo"), [athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_of_athletics "Sport of athletics"), [shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shooting_sports "Shooting sports"), and [karate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate "Karate"). Iran's [National Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Olympic_Committee_of_the_Islamic_Republic_of_Iran "National Olympic Committee of the Islamic Republic of Iran") was founded in 1947.

[Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran "Iran"), formerly known as [Persia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Name_of_Iran "Name of Iran") before 1935 and officially the Islamic Republic of Iran since 1979, first participated in the [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games") in [1900](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_at_the_1900_Summer_Olympics "Iran at the 1900 Summer Olympics"). Iran has sent athletes to compete in every [Summer Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympic_Games "Summer Olympic Games") since [1948](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_at_the_1948_Summer_Olympics "Iran at the 1948 Summer Olympics"), except for [1980](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Summer_Olympics_boycott "1980 Summer Olympics boycott") and [1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Summer_Olympics_boycott "1984 Summer Olympics boycott") due to [political boycotts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boycott "Boycott"). Iran has also participated in the [Winter Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter_Olympic_Games "Winter Olympic Games") on several occasions since [1956](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_at_the_1956_Winter_Olympics "Iran at the 1956 Winter Olympics").

Iran has participated in 19 Summer Olympics and 13 Winter Olympics so far. Iran participated in 9 Summer Olympics and gained 4 gold medals before the [1979 Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iranian_Revolution "Iranian Revolution"), and participated in 10 Summer Olympics and won 23 gold medals after the revolution.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-2)

[Freydoun Malkom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freydoun_Malkom "Freydoun Malkom"), a [fencer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fencing "Fencing") who competed in the [épée](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89p%C3%A9e_(fencing) "Épée (fencing)") event at the [1900 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_at_the_1900_Summer_Olympics "Iran at the 1900 Summer Olympics"), was the first [Iranian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran "Iran") Olympic competitor. [Jafar Salmasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jafar_Salmasi "Jafar Salmasi") won Iran's first Olympic medal in [1948](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_at_the_1948_Summer_Olympics "Iran at the 1948 Summer Olympics"), and [Kimia Alizadeh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimia_Alizadeh "Kimia Alizadeh") was the first Iranian female Olympic medalist, having done so in [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Iran at the 2016 Summer Olympics"). Iranian athletes have won a total of 88 Summer Olympic medals, all in [wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amateur_wrestling "Amateur wrestling"), [weightlifting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_weightlifting "Olympic weightlifting"), [taekwondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taekwondo "Taekwondo"), [athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_of_athletics "Sport of athletics"), [shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shooting_sports "Shooting sports"), and [karate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karate "Karate"). Iran's [National Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Olympic_Committee_of_the_Islamic_Republic_of_Iran "National Olympic Committee of the Islamic Republic of Iran") was founded in 1947.
